title: Hunterian / Royal College of Surgeons: John Thomas Quekett preparations, purchase, teaching catalogue, and surviving address layers

principal_upgrade.previous_state: The slide survey registered the Quekett corpus as REVIEW: 2,500 preparations purchased in 1846 and a much larger current Hunterian slide collection, but the historical teaching/catalogue and surviving address layers had not been integrated.
principal_upgrade.new_state: RCS and project primary-source evidence jointly close the 2,500-preparation purchase, their incorporation into the College's histological museum, Quekett's 1844 annual demonstrations using the collection as an explanatory teaching resource, the 1850 printed histological catalogue, and present survival of Quekett-labelled objects carrying alphanumeric historical marks inside current RCSMS addresses. A secondary object study further identifies five J. W. Bond donations by exact 1850 catalogue numbers, creating a tightly bounded catalogue-to-object S candidate pending direct primary/current-object verification.

grade.bond_five_slide_catalogue_object_crosswa: A++/S-candidate pending direct catalogue-page and object-record inspection

historical_chain.event: Quekett held a three-year studentship in human and comparative anatomy and made the microscopical preparations that formed his large personal/preparatory collection.
The College appointed Quekett to annual demonstrations for the exhibition and connected description of the collection and for explaining methods/resources of microscopical study.
The College purchased Quekett's collection of 2,500 microscopical preparations; the project primary corpus states that it formed part of the histological department of the museum.

Quekett published volume I of the Descriptive and Illustrated Catalogue of the Histological Series in the Museum of the Royal College of Surgeons, giving the collection a printed systematic address layer.

current_surviving_objects.repository: Hunterian Museum / Royal College of Surgeons of England
current_surviving_objects.collection_statement: The current microscope-slide collection contains over 15,000 slides and uses museum identifiers prefixed RCSMS. The official collection page explicitly includes slides prepared by John Thomas Quekett.

bond_selected_crosswalk.attribution_guard: The secondary source describes these as slides donated by J. W. Bond and states that the handwriting is Quekett's. Treat Bond as donor/preparer only to the extent directly supported; do not relabel them as Quekett-made slides simply because Quekett catalogued or labelled them.

address_mechanism.chain: private/preparatory collection -> College purchase -> teaching/demonstration collection -> printed histological catalogue -> alphanumeric object marks -> later institutional cataloguing -> current RCSMS address
address_mechanism.strong_claim: The Hunterian Quekett material shows how a private maker-researcher's preparation corpus became an institutional teaching and catalogue system while older object marks remained legible inside modern museum identifiers.

comparison.qmc: Quekett Microscopical Club assembled heterogeneous member donations and exchange material for circulation.
comparison.hunterian_quekett: The Royal College of Surgeons institutionalized a large bounded preparation corpus through purchase, teaching demonstrations and a printed catalogue.
comparison.cole: Cole's numbered publication slots could survive replacement of individual preparations; the Hunterian case instead preserves layered catalogue and museum addresses on continuing physical objects.

guards: Do not assume every present RCSMS/Quekett object belongs to the exact 2,500-object corpus purchased in 1846 unless object-level provenance establishes this.
Do not treat the current total of 15,000+ microscope slides as the size of Quekett's collection; it is the wider Hunterian slide collection.
Do not identify a present object solely from a similar subject name; retain exact old alphanumeric marks and catalogue wording as the primary crosswalk variables.

The five Bond catalogue/object matches remain A++/S-candidate because the exact crosswalk currently rests on a specialist secondary transcription/reproduction rather than a project-side direct inspection of both primary catalogue pages and current object records.
Do not send a duplicate broad RCS enquiry: MS0027 is already in the project's archive lead queue awaiting substantive response.
